title: Compatible compactification towers with a supplied compactification of the composite
statement: Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{h}Z$ be separated finite-type morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with separatedness and finite type as in [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose given compactifications $d=(i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y,q:\overline Y\to Z)$ of $h$ and $c=(a_0:X\hookrightarrow W,t:W\to Z)$ of $hf$, meaning quasi-compact open first maps [def-weil-open-immersion] and proper second maps [def-weil-proper-morphism]. There exists a compactification $e=(a:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to\overline Y)$ of $if$ and a proper map $v:\overline X\to W$ with $va=a_0$ and $tv=qp$. Put $U=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $b:U\to\overline X$ and $p_Y:U\to Y$. Then $b$ and the induced $c_X:X\to U$ are quasi-compact open immersions, $p_Y$ is proper, $bc_X=a$ and $p_Yc_X=f$. Thus $(c_X,p_Y)$ compactifies $f$, $(a,qp)$ compactifies $hf$, and $p b=i p_Y$ is cartesian. These data base-change to a tower of the same kind under any map $Z'\to Z$. Any two such towers for $f,h$ admit a common refining tower, with compatible proper maps on their ambient compactifications and on their intermediate schemes $U$, commuting with all tower arrows and restricting to the identity on $X,Y$. In particular, a refining tower indexed by $1$ mapping to a tower indexed by $2$ has proper maps $v$ on the ambient compactifications of $X$, $u$ on the ambient compactifications of $Y$, and $w:U_1\to U_2$, with $va_1=a_2$, $ui_1=i_2$, $wc_1=c_2$, $vb_1=b_2w$, $p_2v=up_1$, $p_{Y,2}w=p_{Y,1}$ and $q_2u=q_1$; here $c_1,c_2$ denote the open maps from $X$ to the intermediate schemes. No qcqs hypothesis is imposed on $Z$; existence of the displayed compactifications is part of the data.
